body.p: Tsǃoʼna was just growing at the place Nōʼta. He was alone / Now he just had the name Only-Long-One-Reaching-Up-in-the-World. He was chief at the place Nōʼta. Then he just asked that all / the countries should be made right. Then Tsǃoʼna was asked / by Raven, "What kind of salmon is to be in our river? Is it olachen or perhaps / sockeye, or perhaps spring salmon?“ Then Tsǃoʼna said, "That is not good. / That is not good." Then he was asked, "Are maggots good to be the fish for the place Nōʼta?" Then Tsǃoʼna said, “That is good." / Then Tsǃoʼna thought he would send them away.

Now Tsǃoʼna just went off / and went up. When the fish of the place Nōʼta were finished / he wanted to be chief. He wanted to have the name Only-Long-One-Reaching-Up-in-the-World. Then he went up / to the top of the mountain. He wished to be on top and really he sat down on top of that mountain. Then he became stone / and also his dressed deer skin. Now he spoke when he sat down / on top at the edge of the mountain. He spoke to the later generations, / "You shall shout to me that it may be raining. If anyone wishes to / dry my skins, then you shout to me and ask me to dry my skins and every time it will be a bright day for the later generations."
